correctness.rationale: For every real invertible unit-row matrix B with forest-supported inverse row Gram K, congruence turns the sharp smallest-eigenvalue objective into diagonal(p)-lambda K PSD. A forest-consistent sign vector proves the upper bound 1/T for every p; the signed-edge sum-of-squares explicitly attains it; a zero quadratic form forces any maximizing p to equal the absolute K-row-sum distribution. The Gaussian tree autoregression independently proves SPD and the exact precision entries; the vertex degree-sum identity gives the topology-invariant formula. A standalone extracted verifier checks 51565 exact rational identities, not a finite substitute for the general proof.

value.rationale: A natural full class (unit-row systems with forest-supported inverse row Gram), directly motivated by Gaussian tree graphical models, has an exact unique global optimal sampling rule computable from local precision edges. For arbitrary correlated Gaussian trees, it gives the explicit heterogeneous local law and proves a sharp graph-topology-invariant rate when edge magnitudes are fixed. The difference from the standard uniform rule is meaningful for branching trees, and the solution removes an SDP for an infinite family rather than tabulating an arbitrary small case.
